# AI evaluation results (generated by run_eval.py report)

**Developer-scored.** The prompt set was written and every reply was scored by the L.A.R.A development team, not by teachers or an adviser. These pass rates are not validated by educators.

* Prompt set: version 3, 78 prompts, 33 of them typed in Filipino or Taglish (the right reply is the rule 6 decline line; socratic shape is not scored on them)
* Hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 7535HS with Radeon Graphics, 12 logical CPUs, 15.2 GB RAM, Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0
* llama-server: version: 0.7.0-dev (build 11938, commit 19cce6919) | built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64; settings: {"context_tokens_per_slot": 2048, "prompt_budget": "model tokenizer (llama-server /tokenize)", "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0.2, "seed": 42, "gpu_layers": 0, "threads": 4}
* Scorers: scorer_a, scorer_b; agreement rate 306/381 (80%) of criterion cells (no_direct_answer 97/106 (92%), grounded 64/106 (60%), socratic_shape 42/63 (67%), language 103/106 (97%))

## Rulings on agreed cells

## First token by lesson length

Criterion 5 is judged on the `short` rows (the Lead, #73, 2026-11-13): first token under 10 s for 95% of replies with 2 learners at once. The `long` rows are a known limit, recorded with their times: the Hub reads the whole lesson part before it writes, and sending less lesson text can be tried after the defense.

| qwen3-reap-15b | 1 | short | 64 | 3559 | 5153 | 64/64 (100%) |

## Automated cross-check (not a score)

`score_claude.csv` was scored by Claude on the same blind sheet, after both human sheets were done. It is not in any pass rate above and settles no disagreement (the Lead, #73, 2026-11-09).

* It agrees with the final human verdict on 335/381 (88%) cells.
* 0 cells not compared: the two scorers still disagree.
* The 46 cells where it differs are listed in `cross_check.csv`.
